title: Fathom vs PostHog
description: Fathom vs PostHog — compare cookieless hosted web analytics for marketing sites against product analytics with session replay, feature flags, and experiments.
verdict: Fathom is a privacy-first web analytics product for marketing sites that need clean traffic and goal reports. PostHog is a product analytics suite for teams that need events, funnels, retention, session replay, feature flags, and experiments.
quickAnswer: **Fathom** is the better fit if you need **simple, privacy-respecting website analytics**. **PostHog** is the better fit if you need **in-product behavior, flags, experiments, and session replay** — and you are willing to invest in event instrumentation.
bottomLine: Do not treat these as peers unless you only need pageviews. For blogs and marketing sites, Fathom wins on simplicity, cookieless posture, and a light script. For product-led SaaS, PostHog wins on capability. Hosted Fathom starts at $15/month for 100K pageviews ([Fathom pricing](https://usefathom.com/pricing), checked 2026-11-19). PostHog Cloud includes 1M analytics events and 5K session recordings free every month, then usage-based pricing ([PostHog pricing](https://posthog.com/pricing), checked 2026-11-19).

faq.question: Can Fathom replace PostHog?
faq.answer: No for product teams. Fathom does not offer feature flags, experiments, session replay, or deep retention/cohort product analytics. It covers marketing-site traffic, UTMs, events, and revenue tracking ([Fathom pricing](https://usefathom.com/pricing), checked 2026-11-19).

faq.question: Can PostHog replace Fathom?
faq.answer: For basic website traffic, yes — but it is usually overkill. If you only need referrers and pageviews, Fathom is simpler and designed as cookieless privacy analytics ([Fathom](https://usefathom.com/), checked 2026-11-19). PostHog’s free Cloud tier can cover light event volume, but autocapture, identified users, and replay increase privacy review surface.

faq.question: Which is better for a SaaS marketing site plus app?
faq.answer: Common pattern: Fathom (or similar) on the marketing site and PostHog in the product. Some teams run PostHog everywhere; weigh script weight, event taxonomy cost, and privacy review. See also Google Analytics vs PostHog and PostHog vs Plausible.

faq.question: Which is more privacy-friendly?
faq.answer: Fathom is designed as cookieless privacy-first web analytics and states no cookie banner is required for its tracking ([Fathom](https://usefathom.com/), checked 2026-11-19). PostHog can be configured carefully and offers US/EU Cloud regions, but product analytics features (identified users, session replay) expand what you collect ([PostHog pricing](https://posthog.com/pricing), checked 2026-11-19).

faq.question: Can either be self-hosted?
faq.answer: Hosted Fathom Analytics is cloud-only; Fathom Lite is a separate free self-hosted option with fewer features and no vendor support ([Fathom Lite](https://usefathom.com/pricing/lite), checked 2026-11-19). PostHog offers an MIT open-source self-host path; PostHog’s docs note self-hosted deployments are unsupported and paid-plan features are Cloud-only ([PostHog self-host docs](https://posthog.com/docs/self-host), checked 2026-11-19).

faq.question: I mainly need session replay — is PostHog enough?
faq.answer: PostHog includes session replay on Cloud (5K recordings/month on the free allowance, then usage-based) ([PostHog pricing](https://posthog.com/pricing), checked 2026-11-19). If your primary job is heatmaps and replay on a marketing site rather than product analytics, also look at Hotjar — see our Hotjar tool profile and PostHog vs Hotjar. Fathom does not offer session replay.

editorialNotes.title: Category mismatch is the point
editorialNotes.content: Founders often search **Fathom vs PostHog** when deciding whether a simple analytics tool is enough. If your questions are product questions (activation, retention, flags), Fathom will feel empty quickly. If your questions are traffic questions, PostHog will feel heavy.

editorialNotes.title: Pricing checked today
editorialNotes.content: Fathom entry pricing and PostHog free-tier allowances were checked on 2026-11-19 against [Fathom pricing](https://usefathom.com/pricing) and [PostHog pricing](https://posthog.com/pricing/). Usage-based PostHog costs depend on events, recordings, and flags — use each vendor’s calculator before you commit.
